newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-COCOA COULD PUSH HIGHER, EYE ON CURRENCY.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-COCOA COULD PUSH HIGHER, EYE ON CURRENCY.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures look to be gathering pace after bouncing off last month's troughs but the focus of attention is still likely to be on currency movements, traders and analysts said on Monday.
London's nearby September contract, denominated in sterling, ended firmer on Friday but off the highs reached when the pound slumped against the dollar.
Both traders and analysts said the fortunes of sterling would hold the key for at least the early part of Monday's activity.
The London market was called to open four stg higher than Friday's close.
Currency dealers said sterling made a steady start in Europe, slightly firmer from Friday's lows against the dollar and mark, but was still prone to further weakness.
Sterling, hit hard by official indications that further British interest rate rises were off the menu in the near future, tumbled on heavy selling on Friday and hit a 10-month low against the dollar.
The UK's Producer Price Index figures for July are due to be released at 0830 GMT.

In cocoa, technical analysts said September's short-term momentum indicators were heading higher, suggesting that the market was gathering pace for a possible assault on last month's peaks -- 1,044, 1,052 and then 1,063 stg.
"While two days previously we were looking for a test of 965 we could be seeing the market head up for a test at 1,030...and up to 1,063," said Darren Gurner, technical analyst at Sucden.
"I think it's currency (in London) more than anything else," he said.
Resistance to any push higher would also come from September's 30-day moving average at 1,031, followed by the 40-day average at 1,056 stg.
